reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history, bidding 20 guarantees allocation and yields zero profit; any lower bid risks losing and also yields zero if the opponent bids 20.

Matching B’s repeated 20 preserves half the resource with zero profit; undercutting wins more share but earns positive profit, so a profitable deviation may be attractive. With no final round disclosed, maintain the observed rate this round.

B has matched 20 for the last three rounds. Matching preserves the tie and yields zero, but lowering would forfeit the resource without improving profit; bidding 20 keeps open the chance B lowers and A earns zero either way if B stays at 20.
A has repeatedly chosen 20. Matching would split the resource for zero profit; bidding 19 wins if A stays at 20 and earns 1. If A lowers its rate, this may lose, but the repeated pattern favors 19.
B has matched 20 repeatedly, so lowering risks losing the resource while matching yields zero profit. With no known final round, keep the maximum rate.

B matched 19 after my test and has otherwise used 19 or 20. Matching 19 secures half the resource for 0.5 profit; bidding 20 risks zero profit, while undercutting gives up the resource.
A shifted from 20 to 19 after my 20, then matched my 19 and both earned 0.5. Matching 19 preserves a chance to split the resource profitably; bidding 20 risks returning to zero-profit competition.
